paragraphs.text: And he arose from thence and cometh into the borders of Judaea and beyond the Jordan: and multitudes come together unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἀναστὰς ἔρχεται εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ συμπορεύονται πάλιν ὄχλοι πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ὡς εἰώθει πάλιν ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ekeithen anastas erchetai eis ta horia tēs Ioudaias kai peran tou Iordanou, kai symporeuontai palin ochloi pros auton, kai hōs eiōthei palin edidasken autous.

paragraphs.text: And there came unto him Pharisees, and asked him, Is it lawful for a man to put away [his] wife? trying him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνδρὶ γυναῖκα ἀπολῦσαι, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai epērōtōn auton ei exestin andri gynaika apolysai, peirazontes auton.

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said unto them, What did Moses command you?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί ὑμῖν ἐνετείλατο Μωϋσῆς;
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen autois· Ti hymin eneteilato Mōysēs;

paragraphs.text: And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put her away.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἐπέτρεψεν Μωϋσῆς βιβλίον ἀποστασίου γράψαι καὶ ἀπολῦσαι.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eipan· Epetrepsen Mōysēs biblion apostasiou grapsai kai apolysai.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus said unto them, For your hardness of heart he wrote you this commandment.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πρὸς τὴν σκληροκαρδίαν ὑμῶν ἔγραψεν ὑμῖν τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην·
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen autois· Pros tēn sklērokardian hymōn egrapsen hymin tēn entolēn tautēn·

paragraphs.text: But from the beginning of the creation, Male and female made he them.
paragraphs.original: ἀπὸ δὲ ἀρχῆς κτίσεως ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς·
paragraphs.translit: apo de archēs ktiseōs arsen kai thēly epoiēsen autous·

paragraphs.text: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife;
paragraphs.original: ἕνεκεν τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ προσκολληθήσεται πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: heneken toutou kataleipsei anthrōpos ton patera autou kai tēn mētera kai proskollēthēsetai pros tēn gynaika autou,

paragraphs.text: and the two shall become one flesh: so that they are no more two, but one flesh.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν· ὥστε οὐκέτι εἰσὶν δύο ἀλλὰ μία σάρξ·
paragraphs.translit: kai esontai hoi dyo eis sarka mian· hōste ouketi eisin dyo alla mia sarx·

paragraphs.text: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
paragraphs.original: ὃ οὖν ὁ θεὸς συνέζευξεν ἄνθρωπος μὴ χωριζέτω.
paragraphs.translit: ho oun ho theos synezeuxen anthrōpos mē chōrizetō.

paragraphs.text: And in the house the disciples asked him again of this matter.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν πάλιν οἱ μαθηταὶ περὶ τούτου ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eis tēn oikian palin hoi mathētai peri toutou epērōtōn auton.

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto them, Whosoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her:
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται ἐπʼ αὐτήν,
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· Hos an apolysē tēn gynaika autou kai gamēsē allēn moichatai epʼ autēn,

paragraphs.text: and if she herself shall put away her husband, and marry another, she committeth adultery.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν αὐτὴ ἀπολύσασα τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς γαμήσῃ ἄλλον μοιχᾶται.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean autē apolysasa ton andra autēs gamēsē allon moichatai.

paragraphs.text: And they were bringing unto him little children, that he should touch them: and the disciples rebuked them.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσέφερον αὐτῷ παιδία ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅψηται· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai prosepheron autō paidia hina autōn hapsētai· hoi de mathētai epetimēsan autois.

paragraphs.text: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me; forbid them not: for to such belongeth the kingdom of God.
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠγανάκτησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με, μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: idōn de ho Iēsous ēganaktēsen kai eipen autois· Aphete ta paidia erchesthai pros me, mē kōlyete auta, tōn gar toioutōn estin hē basileia tou theou.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall in no wise enter therein.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō hymin, hos an mē dexētai tēn basileian tou theou hōs paidion, ou mē eiselthē eis autēn.

paragraphs.text: And he took them in his arms, and blessed them, laying his hands upon them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐναγκαλισάμενος αὐτὰ κατευλόγει τιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐπʼ αὐτά.
paragraphs.translit: kai enankalisamenos auta kateulogei titheis tas cheiras epʼ auta.

paragraphs.text: And as he was going forth into the way, there ran one to him, and kneeled to him, and asked him, Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ εἰς ὁδὸν προσδραμὼν εἷς καὶ γονυπετήσας αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσω ἵνα ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;
paragraphs.translit: Kai ekporeuomenou autou eis hodon prosdramōn heis kai gonypetēsas auton epērōta auton· Didaskale agathe, ti poiēsō hina zōēn aiōnion klēronomēsō;

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good save one, [even] God.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen autō· Ti me legeis agathon; oudeis agathos ei mē heis ho theos.

paragraphs.text: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not kill, Do not commit adultery, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Do not defraud, Honor thy father and mother.
paragraphs.original: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ φονεύσῃς, Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Μὴ ἀποστερήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα.
paragraphs.translit: tas entolas oidas· Mē phoneusēs, Mē moicheusēs, Mē klepsēs, Mē pseudomartyrēsēs, Mē aposterēsēs, Tima ton patera sou kai tēn mētera.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, Teacher, all these things have I observed from my youth.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα πάντα ἐφυλαξάμην ἐκ νεότητός μου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de ephē autō· Didaskale, tauta panta ephylaxamēn ek neotētos mou.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus looking upon him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ἠγάπησεν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἕν σε ὑστερεῖ· ὕπαγε ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ δὸς τοῖς πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous emblepsas autō ēgapēsen auton kai eipen autō· Hen se hysterei· hypage hosa echeis pōlēson kai dos tois ptōchois, kai hexeis thēsauron en ouranō, kai deuro akolouthei moi.

paragraphs.text: But his countenance fell at the saying, and he went away sorrowful: for he was one that had great possessions.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ στυγνάσας ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ἀπῆλθεν λυπούμενος, ἦν γὰρ ἔχων κτήματα πολλά.
paragraphs.translit: ho de stygnasas epi tō logō apēlthen lypoumenos, ēn gar echōn ktēmata polla.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus looked round about, and saith unto his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
paragraphs.original: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελεύσονται.
paragraphs.translit: Kai periblepsamenos ho Iēsous legei tois mathētais autou· Pōs dyskolōs hoi ta chrēmata echontes eis tēn basileian tou theou eiseleusontai.

paragraphs.text: And the disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answereth again, and saith unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τέκνα, πῶς δύσκολόν ἐστιν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν·
paragraphs.translit: hoi de mathētai ethambounto epi tois logois autou. ho de Iēsous palin apokritheis legei autois· Tekna, pōs dyskolon estin eis tēn basileian tou theou eiselthein·

paragraphs.text: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle`s eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
paragraphs.original: εὐκοπώτερόν ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τῆς τρυμαλιᾶς τῆς ῥαφίδος διελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: eukopōteron estin kamēlon dia tēs trymalias tēs rhaphidos dielthein ē plousion eis tēn basileian tou theou eiselthein.

paragraphs.text: And they were astonished exceedingly, saying unto him, Then who can be saved?
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;
paragraphs.translit: hoi de perissōs exeplēssonto legontes pros heautous· Kai tis dynatai sōthēnai;

paragraphs.text: Jesus looking upon them saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for all things are possible with God.
paragraphs.original: ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει· Παρὰ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατον ἀλλʼ οὐ παρὰ θεῷ, πάντα γὰρ δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: emblepsas autois ho Iēsous legei· Para anthrōpois adynaton allʼ ou para theō, panta gar dynata para tō theō.

paragraphs.text: Peter began to say unto him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee.
paragraphs.original: Ἤρξατο λέγειν ὁ Πέτρος αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν πάντα καὶ ἠκολουθήκαμέν σοι.
paragraphs.translit: Ērxato legein ho Petros autō· Idou hēmeis aphēkamen panta kai ēkolouthēkamen soi.

paragraphs.text: Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or mother, or father, or children, or lands, for my sake, and for the gospel`s sake,
paragraphs.original: ἔφη ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ ἀδελφὰς ἢ μητέρα ἢ πατέρα ἢ τέκνα ἢ ἀγροὺς ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ ἕνεκεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου,
paragraphs.translit: ephē ho Iēsous· Amēn legō hymin, oudeis estin hos aphēken oikian ē adelphous ē adelphas ē mētera ē patera ē tekna ē agrous heneken emou kai heneken tou euangeliou,

paragraphs.text: but he shall receive a hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν μὴ λάβῃ ἑκατονταπλασίονα νῦν ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ οἰκίας καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφὰς καὶ μητέρας καὶ τέκνα καὶ ἀγροὺς μετὰ διωγμῶν, καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
paragraphs.translit: ean mē labē hekatontaplasiona nyn en tō kairō toutō oikias kai adelphous kai adelphas kai mēteras kai tekna kai agrous meta diōgmōn, kai en tō aiōni tō erchomenō zōēn aiōnion.

paragraphs.text: But many [that are] first shall be last; and the last first.
paragraphs.original: πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι.
paragraphs.translit: polloi de esontai prōtoi eschatoi kai hoi eschatoi prōtoi.

paragraphs.text: And they were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going before them: and they were amazed; and they that followed were afraid. And he took again the twelve, and began to tell them the things that were to happen unto him,
paragraphs.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἀναβαίνοντες εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ἦν προάγων αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο, οἱ δὲ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἐφοβοῦντο. καὶ παραλαβὼν πάλιν τοὺς δώδεκα ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς λέγειν τὰ μέλλοντα αὐτῷ συμβαίνειν
paragraphs.translit: Ēsan de en tē hodō anabainontes eis Hierosolyma, kai ēn proagōn autous ho Iēsous, kai ethambounto, hoi de akolouthountes ephobounto. kai paralabōn palin tous dōdeka ērxato autois legein ta mellonta autō symbainein

paragraphs.text: [saying], Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests and the scribes; and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him unto the Gentiles:
paragraphs.original: ὅτι Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς γραμματεῦσιν, καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν θανάτῳ καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν
paragraphs.translit: hoti Idou anabainomen eis Hierosolyma, kai ho hyios tou anthrōpou paradothēsetai tois archiereusin kai tois grammateusin, kai katakrinousin auton thanatō kai paradōsousin auton tois ethnesin

paragraphs.text: and they shall mock him, and shall spit upon him, and shall scourge him, and shall kill him; and after three days he shall rise again.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐμπαίξουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐμπτύσουσιν αὐτῷ καὶ μαστιγώσουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν, καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai empaixousin autō kai emptysousin autō kai mastigōsousin auton kai apoktenousin, kai meta treis hēmeras anastēsetai.

paragraphs.text: And there come near unto him James and John, the sons of Zebedee, saying unto him, Teacher, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall ask of thee.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσπορεύονται αὐτῷ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης οἱ υἱοὶ Ζεβεδαίου λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἵνα ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσωμέν σε ποιήσῃς ἡμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai prosporeuontai autō Iakōbos kai Iōannēs hoi hyioi Zebedaiou legontes autō· Didaskale, thelomen hina ho ean aitēsōmen se poiēsēs hēmin.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, What would ye that I should do for you?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν;
paragraphs.translit: ho de eipen autois· Ti thelete poiēsō hymin;

paragraphs.text: And they said unto him, Grant unto us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and one on [thy] left hand, in thy glory.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δὸς ἡμῖν ἵνα εἷς σου ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ ἀριστερῶν καθίσωμεν ἐν τῇ δόξῃ σου.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eipan autō· Dos hēmin hina heis sou ek dexiōn kai heis ex aristerōn kathisōmen en tē doxē sou.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus said unto them, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink the cup that I drink? or to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε· δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω, ἢ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθῆναι;
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous eipen autois· Ouk oidate ti aiteisthe· dynasthe piein to potērion ho egō pinō, ē to baptisma ho egō baptizomai baptisthēnai;

paragraphs.text: And they said unto him, We are able. And Jesus said unto them, The cup that I drink ye shall drink; and with the baptism that I am baptized withal shall ye be baptized:
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Δυνάμεθα. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ πίνω πίεσθε καὶ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐγὼ βαπτίζομαι βαπτισθήσεσθε,
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eipan autō· Dynametha. ho de Iēsous eipen autois· To potērion ho egō pinō piesthe kai to baptisma ho egō baptizomai baptisthēsesthe,

paragraphs.text: but to sit on my right hand or on [my] left hand is not mine to give; but [it is for them] for whom it hath been prepared.
paragraphs.original: τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου ἢ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλʼ οἷς ἡτοίμασται.
paragraphs.translit: to de kathisai ek dexiōn mou ē ex euōnymōn ouk estin emon dounai, allʼ hois hētoimastai.

paragraphs.text: And when the ten heard it, they began to be moved with indignation concerning James and John.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἤρξαντο ἀγανακτεῖν περὶ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάννου.
paragraphs.translit: Kai akousantes hoi deka ērxanto aganaktein peri Iakōbou kai Iōannou.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus called them to him, and saith unto them, Ye know that they who are accounted to rule over the Gentiles lord it over them; and their great ones exercise authority over them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ δοκοῦντες ἄρχειν τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι αὐτῶν κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai proskalesamenos autous ho Iēsous legei autois· Oidate hoti hoi dokountes archein tōn ethnōn katakyrieuousin autōn kai hoi megaloi autōn katexousiazousin autōn.

paragraphs.text: But it is not so among you: but whosoever would become great among you, shall be your minister;
paragraphs.original: οὐχ οὕτως δέ ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν· ἀλλʼ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ μέγας γενέσθαι ἐν ὑμῖν, ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος,
paragraphs.translit: ouch houtōs de estin en hymin· allʼ hos an thelē megas genesthai en hymin, estai hymōn diakonos,

paragraphs.text: and whosoever would be first among you, shall be servant of all.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος, ἔσται πάντων δοῦλος·
paragraphs.translit: kai hos an thelē en hymin einai prōtos, estai pantōn doulos·

paragraphs.text: For the Son of man also came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai gar ho hyios tou anthrōpou ouk ēlthen diakonēthēnai alla diakonēsai kai dounai tēn psychēn autou lytron anti pollōn.

paragraphs.text: And they come to Jericho: and as he went out from Jericho, with his disciples and a great multitude, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the way side.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἰεριχώ. καὶ ἐκπορευομένου αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλου ἱκανοῦ ὁ υἱὸς Τιμαίου Βαρτιμαῖος τυφλὸς προσαίτης ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai erchontai eis Ierichō. kai ekporeuomenou autou apo Ierichō kai tōn mathētōn autou kai ochlou hikanou ho hyios Timaiou Bartimaios typhlos prosaitēs ekathēto para tēn hodon.

paragraphs.text: And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out, and say, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζαρηνός ἐστιν ἤρξατο κράζειν καὶ λέγειν· Υἱὲ Δαυὶδ Ἰησοῦ, ἐλέησόν με.
paragraphs.translit: kai akousas hoti Iēsous ho Nazarēnos estin ērxato krazein kai legein· Hyie Dauid Iēsou, eleēson me.

paragraphs.text: And many rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried out the more a great deal, Thou son of David, have mercy on me.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ πολλοὶ ἵνα σιωπήσῃ· ὁ δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.
paragraphs.translit: kai epetimōn autō polloi hina siōpēsē· ho de pollō mallon ekrazen· Hyie Dauid, eleēson me.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus stood still, and said, Call ye him. And they call the blind man, saying unto him, Be of good cheer: rise, he calleth thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Φωνήσατε αὐτόν. καὶ φωνοῦσι τὸν τυφλὸν λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Θάρσει, ἔγειρε, φωνεῖ σε.
paragraphs.translit: kai stas ho Iēsous eipen· Phōnēsate auton. kai phōnousi ton typhlon legontes autō· Tharsei, egeire, phōnei se.

paragraphs.text: And he, casting away his garment, sprang up, and came to Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποβαλὼν τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ ἀναπηδήσας ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apobalōn to himation autou anapēdēsas ēlthen pros ton Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answered him, and said, What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? And the blind man said unto him, Rabboni, that I may receive my sight.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω; ὁ δὲ τυφλὸς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ραββουνι, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis autō ho Iēsous eipen· Ti soi theleis poiēsō; ho de typhlos eipen autō· Rabbouni, hina anablepsō.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And straightway he received his sight, and followed him in the way.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὕπαγε, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε. καὶ εὐθὺς ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho Iēsous eipen autō· Hypage, hē pistis sou sesōken se. kai euthys aneblepsen, kai ēkolouthei autō en tē hodō.
